messages.content: RoboRide announces 24/7 coverage, 5 minute average wait, $0.10 per mile. Autonomous delivery service also launched. Second robotaxi competitor enters Millfield market.
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Auto sector revenue index: 75 (baseline: 100). Foot traffic and sales are somewhat down.
People around you are stressed: Betty Kowalski. The mood is tense.

You heard directly from Carlos Ruiz (Master Mechanic): Contact the fleet operator who Sarah Kim reached on my behalf. Follow up directly — not through Sarah, in my own name. Introduce myself properly, reference the call, ask whether there is value in meeting to understand what their EV service needs look like as their fleet expands. This is not a job application. It is a professional introduction. The difference matters to how I carry myself going in.

You heard directly from Carlos Ruiz (Master Mechanic): Schedule coffee with Angela Wright. She offered. She is stressed. I am not going to manage this relationship from a distance — I am going to show up as a person, not as a professional contact. Bring nothing to sell. Ask real questions about how she is doing and what she is navigating. Let whatever professional value exists in the connection emerge from the human conversation, not from an agenda I carry in.

You heard directly from Sarah Kim (Junior Mechanic): After sitting for the assessment — regardless of the result but especially if I pass — send a follow-up message to the contact at Millfield Regional Fleet Service. Short, direct: I took the EVT Level 1 assessment, I am expecting results within two weeks, and I wanted to honor the timeline I mentioned when we spoke. Ask whether there is a good time to reconnect once the cert is confirmed. This is not a job application. It is a relationship maintenance signal to someone who has already invested 22 minutes in a conversation with me.
